title: 10 Summer Meditations For Next School Year https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2014/06/21/10-summer-meditations-for-next-school-year/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin uses the summer break as an opportunity to offer ten short, focused meditations that together form a framework for exceptional classroom management. Each meditation—consistency, routines, modeling, temperament, speaking, personality, observation, humor, pace, and breathing—is explained with a brief rationale for its behavioral impact, from consistency building trust and rapport to a calm morning breathing ritual reducing stress and improving effectiveness. He emphasizes that these principles work together to create a classroom students look forward to, rather than functioning as a checklist of individual techniques. The article closes with a broader philosophical point: effective classroom management isn't about doing more, adding systems, or trying harder, but about relationships, good instruction, honesty, and simplicity—doing less, better.
points: Consistency in behavior, tone, and follow-through is the foundation for trust, rapport, and a well-behaved classroom.
Every repeatable school-day moment should become a taught routine students can perform independently.
Calm, easygoing temperament settles students and gives the teacher an effortless leadership presence.
Stepping back to observe rather than hovering after instruction builds student independence and attentiveness.
Effective classroom management is about doing less, better—relationships, clarity, and simplicity—not adding more systems or effort.
quotes: Summer provides an opportunity to push the reset button, to reflect on the previous year and make resolutions for the next.
Consistency in your behavior, in your interactions with students, in your speaking and temperament, and in your follow-through is critical to creating a happy, well-behaved classroom.
Every repeatable moment of the school day should be made into a routine your students can perform without your assistance.
Maintaining a calm, easygoing demeanor settles students, removes excitability, and gives you the effortless leadership presence your students will want to follow.
One of the maxims of Smart Classroom Management is to never move on until you’re getting exactly what you want from your students.
Effective classroom management isn’t about doing more. It isn’t about talking more, moving faster, or trying harder.
It’s about relationships. It’s about good instruction. It’s about being real and clear and direct. It’s about love and laughter.
